reason: Real: every symbol outside NSE/BSE raises ProviderError (corporate_disclosures.py:392-393), and the router maps that to HTTP 502 (routers/disclosures.py:69,90,111). An out-of-scope instrument is reported as an upstream failure, and no ADR ownership lane exists. Corrections: the message is literally accurate (SIFY is not an NSE/BSE instrument). No frontend panel calls these routes (the only consumers are the agent tools at disclosure_tools.py:53-54,75-76, which pass it on as 'provider error', and ownership_check, which returns None). The pack itself records the Indian shareholding pattern as a world_gap. The result is a mislabelled error plus a missing 20-F ownership fallback, not a high-severity core-flow break, so the severity is lowered to medium.
evidence_checked: Opened the disclosures service lane gate, the router exception mapping, the agent-tool wrappers and ownership_check. grep of src/ found no frontend consumer of /disclosures/*. Re-ran all three GETs against :52152 on 2026-09-23: all return HTTP 502 with the cited details.
repro_check: curl -s -w '%{http_code}' '127.0.0.1:52152/disclosures/shareholding?symbol=SIFY' (and /announcements, /results) -> 502 {detail: "disclosures: 'SIFY' is not a known NSE/BSE instrument"} / nse_direct variant.

reason: The symptom reproduces, but the stated mechanism is wrong. The name matcher does scan the US master (symbol_resolver.py:754-755), and SIFY scores higher than every Indian row (fuzzy 0.913 against 0.80 for ASMTEC). The real cause: the stray '(ADR)' token keeps the query out of the name-exact and canonical bands, so every row lands in BAND_FUZZY. There the sort key (band, locale_rank, score) at :763 ranks all IN-locale rows above a better-scoring US row under an IN session, and _MAX_CANDIDATES=6 (:115) truncates SIFY off the list. 'Sify Technologies', 'Sify Technologies Ltd' and 'Sify Technologies Limited' all bind SIFY at 1.0, and region US/GLOBAL puts SIFY first. Nothing binds wrongly (needs_disambiguation is true), so the severity is lowered to medium. The general defect is that within the fuzzy band the locale key buries a clearly better foreign match entirely rather than just ordering it lower.
evidence_checked: Opened the tokenizer, _name_score, _locale_rank and the banded match/sort. Called _name_score directly in the sidecar venv: SIFY (0, 0.913) vs ASMTEC (0, 0.80). resolve(q,'US') and resolve(q,'GLOBAL') both put SIFY first. Probed :52152 /resolve with 6 name variants on 2026-09-23.
repro_check: curl '127.0.0.1:52152/resolve?q=Sify+Technologies+Ltd+%28ADR%29' -> 6 BSE candidates, no SIFY; same without '(ADR)' -> resolved SIFY 1.0; symbol_resolver.resolve(q,'GLOBAL') -> ['SIFY','ASMTEC',...].

reason: The former_name half is refuted. Instrument.former_name is defined as 'the retired symbol, when answered as its renamed form' (symbol_resolver.py:239) and is filled only from the NSE symbol-change lane (:896). It is a former TICKER, not a former legal name, and SIFY's NASDAQ ticker has not changed, so null is correct for that field. The remaining gap holds: the identity payload has no field for former legal names, board/listing tier or listing date, and the US master carries only [ticker, name]. That is a low-severity identity-history gap.
evidence_checked: Opened the Instrument dataclass, the US master loader and _enrich_instrument, and inspected the us_instruments.json row for SIFY. The collected resolve body at collected/P17_SIFY.json:19-31 matches.
repro_check: curl '127.0.0.1:52152/resolve?q=SIFY' -> former_name null (by field definition: no ticker rename), no board/listing_date keys in the schema.

reason: ISIN is null, but by documented design for every US instrument, not a lookup failure specific to SIFY. _enrich_instrument (symbol_resolver.py:857-868) joins ISIN only from the BSE master or the India sector map and says outright that US tickers get nothing added; the US master (:345-356) stores only [ticker, name] for all 10,365 rows. It is an honest null with no fabrication risk, and a US ticker is already unambiguous for routing. The severity is lowered to low: a class-wide missing identifier for US rows (add ISIN/CUSIP to the SEC master if cross-source matching needs it).
evidence_checked: Opened the enrichment join and the US master loader, and checked the SIFY row and the row shape in us_instruments.json (10,365 rows, 2 columns).
repro_check: curl '127.0.0.1:52152/resolve?q=SIFY' -> isin null; the same holds for any US ticker (e.g. NVDA) because the US master has no ISIN column.

reason: This is partly wrong. dividend_per_share_ttm is a derived field that /fundamentals deliberately does not stamp (yfinance_provider.py:167-181, and the collected payload has no field_meta for it). The research FAST leg does compute it: _apply_dividend_ttm sets 0.0 with the label 'no dividends paid (trailing 12m)' on affirmed_zero (research/fast.py:207-224), and get_dividend_ttm('SIFY') returns affirmed_zero today. The gap that remains is narrower: on the /fundamentals route and the Equity Overview panel, dividend_yield and dividend_per_share show 'provider did not publish this field' even though Yahoo publishes trailingAnnualDividendRate 0.0, which the mapping ignores (yfinance_provider.py:347-351,375). No last-declared dividend (2019) is exposed anywhere. Severity stays low.
